# Cavelon Documentation

> The documentation of this Cavelon instance (version v0.0.0-dev) as markdown. Each link returns one page. A link inside a page to /docs/<section>/<slug> names the page at https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/<section>/<slug>.md.

## Welcome

- [What is Cavelon](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/welcome/overview.md): The mental model behind Cavelon — organizations, solutions, agent graphs, shared capabilities, and entry points — and how a run flows end to end.
- [Platform Guide](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/welcome/platform-guide.md): A tour of every Cavelon building block — the layered architecture, what each layer contributes, and three complete solution blueprints.
- [Start Here](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/welcome/start-here.md): Five guided reading paths through the Cavelon docs — pick the one that matches your role and follow it page by page
- [Role Workflows](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/welcome/role-workflows.md): The main configuration and day-to-day workflows for Tenant Owners, Builders, Operators, Analysts, Members, and platform roles.
- [Dashboard Tour](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/welcome/dashboard-tour.md): A guided tour of the Cavelon admin dashboard — the layout, the five places, tenant and platform worlds, and the command palette
- [Bot Setup and the Guided Experience](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/welcome/bot-setup-and-essential-mode.md): The guided, AI-assisted way to configure a Cavelon bot — the Persona Wizard and Harness Architect — and when to use it versus the full pages

## Quick Start

- [Your First Chatbot](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/quickstart/first-chatbot.md): From an empty tenant to a bot that sounds like yours — the workspace, the solution boundary, and the persona layer, in one sitting.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorial Track Overview](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/overview.md): A guided, hands-on learning path that builds from a single knowledge-base bot to a full enterprise harness, one tutorial at a time
- [Harness Graph Guide](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/harness-graph-guide.md): The beginner's orientation to the harness graph — the six data rails, the two kinds of node, three hand-walked builds, the Node Workbench, and a cheat sheet.
- [Build with the Harness Architect](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/build-with-the-architect.md): Describe a change in plain language, review it, apply it, have the Architect try it, and publish — the whole loop in one sitting
- [Patterns Cookbook](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/patterns-cookbook.md): Ten proven harness patterns — from responsive chat with a deep-research lane to trigger pipelines with human approval gates — and how to pick the right one for your use-case.
- [Build a Simple KB Chatbot](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/simple-kb-chatbot.md): Build "Acme Support" — a single agent grounded in one knowledge base, answering with citations, tuned for retrieval quality, tested, and embedded
- [Build a Multi-Agent Support Bot](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/multi-agent-support-bot.md): Grow the single-agent Acme bot into a triage graph that hands off to Billing and Technical specialists, with a shared persona and guardrails
- [Give an Agent a Tool](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/tool-using-agent.md): Build a webhook tool that looks up live order status from a REST API, store its credential as a tenant secret, assign it to an agent, test it in the Playground, and bind a platform tool template
- [Give your agent a calculator](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/agent-calculator.md): Hands-on — attach the compute tool so an agent does exact arithmetic, dates, and aggregation instead of guessing
- [Send website visitors to the right page or checkout](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/guide-visitors-to-checkout.md): Hands-on — let an agent take a visitor from advice to the matching product page or checkout on your own website, with their choices already filled in
- [Build a Structured-Data Chatbot](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/structured-data-chatbot.md): Back a chatbot with a flat catalog table, configure column roles, get the generated query tools, and render results as a carousel with detail cards
- [Triggers and Agent Runs](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/triggers-and-agent-runs.md): Automate a background workflow with a webhook trigger that seeds Run State from a payload, runs your graph headlessly, and delivers the result via an outbound callback
- [Build an Orchestration Pipeline](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/orchestration-pipelines.md): Build a deterministic document-intake pipeline — trigger, router, a fan-out to parallel specialists reconverging on a join, approval, API Request, output — threading Run State and documents
- [External Approvals from Your Own App](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/hitl-external-approval.md): Build the approval surface in your own product - detect a run paused at an Approval node, decide it server-side over the HITL API, and confirm the resume from run state
- [Shape Data with the Transform Node](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/shape-data-with-transform.md): Reshape a pipeline payload with the Transform node — the three modes, the visual builder, a worked mapping over a list, JSON-mode deep nesting, and output_schema validation
- [Triage and Resolve Incidents](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/triage-and-resolve-incidents.md): Work an incident from unread signal to acknowledged ownership, diagnosis, escalation, resolution, and verified closure without confusing read state with operational state.
- [Send Documents Through a Channel](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/send-documents-through-channels.md): Generate a PDF receipt and deliver it through WhatsApp, with governed outbound media and provider-safe link fallback.
- [Receive a Photo Through a Channel](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/receive-photos-through-a-channel.md): Let a customer send a photo to your bot on WhatsApp and have the agent actually see it — enable per-binding inbound media, use a vision-capable model, and understand what the agent sees.
- [Combine Harnesses with Sub-Workflows](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/combine-harnesses.md): Factor reusable logic into one harness and call it from others with the Harness Call node — the mental model, a worked refund example, the channel-adapter and triage patterns, and the guardrails
- [Connections and Delegated OAuth](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/connections-and-delegated-oauth.md): Build an assistant that acts in real Microsoft 365 or Google systems — first on a shared tenant account, then as each signed-in end user
- [Personal Assistant (Beta)](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/personal-assistant.md): Build a per-user assistant that works with mail, calendar, files, contacts, and tasks through Personal cloud login
- [Enterprise Capstone](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/enterprise-capstone.md): Assemble a governed, authenticated, regression-tested enterprise chatbot — MCP server, governance, end-user auth, a test suite, and a published release.
- [Create and approve a text block](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/first-text-block.md): Hands-on — author a reusable text block, run it through four-eyes approval, and reference it from a transform template with {{baustein:slug}}
- [Author a Solution Library entry](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/author-catalog-workflow.md): Package a tested harness, write a discoverable listing, define setup requirements, run four-eyes approval, and publish it safely
- [Install from the Solution Library](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/apply-catalog-workflow.md): Scout a building block or solution blueprint, inspect its workflow, map tenant resources, preview changes, and install an approved version
- [Air-Gapped, Sovereign Deployment](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/air-gapped-sovereign-deployment.md): A hands-on operator walkthrough to run Cavelon with zero external data flows — point every model role at local endpoints, close the tracing and web-search gaps, and prove no external hop fired.
- [Keep a knowledge base in step with a source system](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/keep-a-knowledge-base-in-step-with-a-source-system.md): Let an external system declare what a corpus should contain, and have the platform converge on that declaration — fetch, verify, publish, and report back
- [Plan Capacity for a Self-Hosted Model](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/plan-model-capacity.md): A worked example — from what your model server can serve to the platform's endpoint limit, run caps and per-tenant caps, then load-test, read the signals and tune
- [Coding Agent on Your Own VM](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/tutorials/coding-agent-with-a-customer-vm.md): A developer pushes a feature spec, CI starts a run, and agents on your VM review it, implement it task by task and publish the branch after approval

## Academy

- [The Harness Track](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/overview.md): The self-paced Cavelon Academy course — from first sandbox to certified harness engineer, one working build per module.
- [How to Get Help](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/getting-help.md): The help ladder for the direct-access Harness Track — Platform Assistant, docs, hint ladders, run evidence, and support.
- [Grading & Certification](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/grading-and-certification.md): How the Harness Track grades your work — behavior suites, the config inspector, the E2E checker — and what the Level 1 certificate requires.
- [Base module: Pre-flight & Foundations (three sittings)](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-0-preflight.md): Provision your sandbox, install the mental model everything hangs on — the agent loop, the harness, the two-layer prompt — then ship a persona-true concierge and grow it into a small team. 7.8 hours.
- [Lesson: Harnesses & the three-layer model](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d0-harnesses.md): What a harness is, the tenant-harness-graph hierarchy, and which assets are harness-bound versus tenant-wide — the boundary you'll navigate throughout the course. 30 minutes.
- [Lesson: Reading traces & choosing models](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d0-traces.md): Read a Playground run trace like an engineer — turns, spans, the composed prompt — pick a model tier per agent role, and codify probes as test suites. 20 minutes.
- [Lesson: Prompt Composition — Persona × Instructions](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d0-prompt-composition.md): The two-layer prompt: Persona owns WHO your bot is across every agent, instructions own WHAT one agent does — and how to route a bug to the right layer. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: The persona clinic](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d0-persona-clinic.md): Give your starter bot an identity, a greeting and a boundary that holds under a second push — then move one rule between Persona and agent instructions and feel which layer owns it. 35 minutes.
- [Lesson: The agent graph](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d0-agent-graph.md): From one agent to a team — the entry agent on the canvas, handoff versus consult, and when a second agent beats a skill. The mental model for everything you build in this module. 50 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — the same team, three ways](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d0-variants.md): Test the team as built, try it collapsed into one agent, then grow it for good — a spa specialist the concierge consults — and run the same three messages through all three. 40 minutes.
- [Challenge 1: The Concierge](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/challenge-1-the-concierge.md): Build a persona-true front-desk bot for Alpenblick Hotels from a written brand brief — no knowledge base, pure persona and instructions. 60 minutes.
- [Module 1: Tools](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-1-tools.md): Give the team hands — the three tool types, webhook tools with secrets, documents and forms, skills that carry a procedure with its tools, the first guardrail, built three ways. About 7.3 hours.
- [Lesson: The tool decision triangle](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d1-tools.md): What a tool is to the model, the builtin–webhook–MCP decision triangle, and why the description on a tool — not its code — is the interface the model reads. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: Wire the concierge to AlpenDesk](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d1-alpendesk-webhook.md): The Module 1 guided build — two webhook tools against the AlpenDesk mock hotel-ops API, with secret auth, a call cap, and a confirmation gate. Every field value stated. 75 minutes.
- [Lesson: Webhook anatomy](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d1-webhooks.md): Dissect a webhook tool definition — method and URL, headers, the parameter schema, {{param}} vs {{secret:key}} resolution, timeouts, honest errors, and the SSRF guard. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: Documents & forms](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d1-documents-forms.md): Two builtins that turn a chatbot into a workflow front-end — generate a real PDF, render a structured intake form instead of asking in prose, and read both arriving in the trace. 40 minutes.
- [Lesson: Skills](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d1-skills.md): A skill bundles instructions, tools and knowledge so any agent picks up a procedure in one assignment. Which layer a rule belongs to, which knowledge-base list wins, and a drill. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: The break-it lab](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d1-break-it.md): Attack your own bot, watch the attack land, assign the prompt-injection detector to the agent the run starts at, and watch the same attack end in the rail's refusal. 20 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — the same hands, three ways](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d1-variants.md): Test the AlpenDesk tools as built, loosen the booking cap on purpose, then share the procedure as a skill on two agents — the booking tool capped on each. 45 minutes.
- [Challenge 2: Close the Loop](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/challenge-2-close-the-loop.md): Prove the AlpenDesk wiring the webhook lab built — reservation lookups and spa bookings with secrets, call caps, and honest failure handling, then one tool built unguided. 80 minutes.
- [Module 2: Knowledge](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-2-knowledge.md): RAG done right — the four-stage retrieval pipeline, honest citations, structured vs vector knowledge bases, and the tuning knobs that matter. About 7.8 hours.
- [Lesson: Knowledge bases & retrieval](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d2-knowledge-bases.md): The road from a library file to a cited answer — ingestion, chunks, hybrid search, and the agent's search tool — plus choosing a KB type and the content-language lever. 30 minutes.
- [Lab: Ingestion — break it and recover](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d2-ingestion.md): Deliberately rough handling of a knowledge base — scrape a single page, copy the Alpenblick pack in, then retire, delete and restore documents until no status surface can surprise you. 30 minutes.
- [Lesson: Retrieval parameters](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d2-retrieval-tuning.md): The three retrieval knobs that matter in this module — survivors after reranking, the score floor that drops garbage, and content language — and how to watch them work. 25 minutes.
- [Lesson: Getting the properties into a structured KB](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d2-structured-kbs.md): Which file a structured KB loads, which section takes it, what the schema import decided about your columns — and the four KB-type calls Challenge 3 asks of you. 15 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — the same twelve houses, three ways](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d2-variants.md): Ask the properties table one question as the structured KB you built, then as a prose KB, and keep the shape that answered right — both on one agent, with a floor you measured. 50 minutes.
- [Challenge 3: Grounded or Nothing](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/challenge-3-grounded-or-nothing.md): Ground the Alpenblick concierge in a messy real-world document pack — cited answers, refused traps, and one curation decision. 105 minutes.
- [Module 3: Pipelines](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-3-pipelines.md): The deterministic rail, one node at a time — Transform, For Each and Output on a seeded pipeline that starts from a Chat Start, with a run to read after every step. About 4.6 hours.
- [Lesson: Nodes, edges and the two rails](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d3-rails.md): Deterministic nodes around your agents: where the runtime decides instead of a model, the payload rail replaced at every hop, the run-state rail that remembers, and the Workbench. 30 minutes.
- [Lab: Your first pipeline](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d3-first-pipeline.md): One pipeline edge from the Chat Start to the Output, one demo run, and the run's answer read back — the smallest deterministic graph that does something, and the loop every lab repeats. 25 minutes.
- [Lesson: Transform](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d3-transform.md): The node that reshapes a payload without a model: its three modes, the four value kinds and the More menu, the one rule about calculations, and the rail-click that writes a path for you. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: Shape the feed](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d3-transform.md): One Transform between the Chat Start and the Output: five rows in four value kinds, a list counted, a string templated, two dotted names nested into an object, and a run read back. 45 minutes.
- [Lesson: For Each](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d3-for-each.md): One pass per item: the loop's source, its body and done branches, the back edge that is the loop, the two ways to address the current item, and wire first, map second. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: One reservation at a time](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d3-for-each.md): A For Each over the reservations, a body lane of two Transforms that returns to the loop, a done lane that collects — built in the order the canvas accepts, then stepped through. 50 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — the same pipeline, three ways](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d3-variants.md): Run the pipeline as built, rebuild its per-item Transform from the JSON view and prove the answer identical, then switch the Chat Start to the VIP and waitlist feed and keep it. 30 minutes.
- [Module 4: The Graph](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-4-the-graph.md): The summit — the Module 3 pipeline learns to branch, remember, run two things at once and survive a poisoned row; then Challenge 4 rebuilds it on a webhook-fed starter, graded. About 7.2 hours.
- [Lesson: Router and condition edges](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d4-router.md): Branching without a model: a Router whose condition rows are checked in priority order with one default; the quote trap; where two lanes may meet again. 30 minutes.
- [Lab: Three lanes](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d4-router.md): A Router inside the loop: VIP guests, the waitlist and everyone else each take a Transform of their own, every lane returns to the loop, and the true-versus-"true" trap is avoided. 45 minutes.
- [Lesson: Run state & the two grammars](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d4-run-state.md): The case file a run carries between nodes, the two spellings of one field — a bare path to write, a lane path to read — and a six-question drill that makes the difference stick. 35 minutes.
- [Lesson: Fan-out, Join and the error edge](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d4-fan-out-join.md): Two things at once: a fan-out that lives on the pipeline edges and the Join that reconverges it; and the error edge, which carries a failure into a recovery lane instead of ending the run. 30 minutes.
- [Lab: Tally and summary at once](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d4-join.md): After the loop, a fan-out: a deterministic tally and the Summary writer reconverging on a Join before the Output; then an error edge inside the loop, so a poisoned row is quarantined. 45 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — remember, keep, break](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d4-variants.md): Run the pipeline as built; a keeper that bridges the export id onto the run-state rail; then both grammars spelled wrong on purpose. 30 minutes.
- [Lab: The debug lab](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d5-debug.md): Five planted bugs that all pass design-time validation — the checker verifies structure, not intent. Taken in run order: the first is walked, the rest solved at their stop. 60 minutes.
- [Challenge 4: The Night Auditor](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/challenge-4-the-night-auditor.md): Turn Alpenblick's nightly reservations feed into an audit report, in stages on a starter canvas — loop and transforms, then routing, then an error edge; fan-out and join optional. 110 minutes.
- [Module 5: Autonomy](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-5-autonomy.md): Autonomy with a leash — triggers that start runs unattended, approvals with real expiry, guardrails against hostile input — and your own refund workflow in three checked stages. About 7.4 hours.
- [Lesson: Triggers](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d5-triggers.md): How a harness runs with nobody in the chat: schedule and webhook triggers, the sample payload, the three-way payload split, sync vs async, and Workflow runs. 30 minutes.
- [Lesson: The HITL map](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d5-hitl.md): Three checks, three deciders — the end user confirms in chat, an operator approves a paused run against a real deadline, a guardrail decides with no human at all. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — the same approval, three ways](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d5-variants.md): Reject an approval with nothing wired after it and read the notice sent in your name, save one with a blank expiry and read the deadline it armed, then keep the routed shape. 65 minutes.
- [Challenge 5: Trust Boundaries](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/challenge-5-trust-boundaries.md): Automate Alpenblick's refund handling with an unattended pipeline a human signs off on — approval with enforced expiry, guardrail on the input, honest delivery. 110 minutes.
- [Module 6: Integration](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-6-integration.md): Own the edges — drive chat over SSE, resolve approvals from your own app via the HITL API, build and connect your own MCP server, embed the widget. About 7.2 hours.
- [Lesson: The chat API & SSE wire contract](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d6-chat-api.md): Drive your harness from your own code — chat-scoped keys, the session lifecycle, and the SSE event stream your client must honor. Same pipeline as the Playground. 25 minutes.
- [Lesson: MCP servers](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d6-mcp.md): One server, many discovered tools: what MCP adds over webhooks, the three transports, and how to register a server and assign it to an agent. 25 minutes.
- [Lab: Build Your Own MCP Server](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-build-your-own-mcp-server.md): Stand up an MCP server from the starter repo — one tool shipped, one you build — connect it over Streamable HTTP, and watch the governance proxy log every call. 60 minutes.
- [Lab: Variants — the same rates tool as MCP and as a webhook](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d6-variants.md): Count what connecting the rates server over MCP made you configure, build the identical call as a webhook tool and count again, then keep the route that grows a second tool for free. 20 minutes.
- [Lab: The widget quick-lab](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lab-d6-widget.md): Embed your Module 2 bot on a plain HTML page, theme it to Alpenblick's brand colour, and decide which of the three Chat User auth methods your capstone needs. 25 minutes.
- [Challenge 6: Mission Control](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/challenge-6-mission-control.md): Build Alpenblick's ops portal — fire the refund workflow, relay approvals server-side over the HITL API, confirm from run state, feed it from your MCP server. 100 minutes.
- [Module 7: Mastery](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/day-7-mastery.md): Patterns, packaging, operations — then seven hours of capstone work and a review-ready demonstration. The module where the course becomes a profession. 11.7 hours.
- [Lesson: Choosing the pattern](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d7-patterns.md): Single agent, specialists, deterministic pipeline, or hybrid — read a brief's job characteristics, pick the shape that matches, and defend the choice in one paragraph. 30 minutes.
- [Lesson: Ship it right — Solution Library & text blocks](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d7-ship-it.md): Ship a proven harness through the Solution Library — versioned, four-eyes reviewed, installed with preview and backup — and govern verbatim wording with text blocks. 20 minutes.
- [Lesson: Operate what you ship](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d7-operate.md): Use Home, Notifications, Incidents, System Email, and Email Channels for the jobs they actually own — a routing drill, then evidence from attention to resolution. 15 minutes.
- [Lesson: Connections](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/lesson-d7-connections.md): Static secrets vs OAuth connections — when a tool acts as the tenant and when as the signed-in user, where connections live, and when production features need them. 15 minutes.
- [Capstone Tracks](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/capstone-tracks.md): Three capstone briefs — the Support Suite, the Back-Office Automator, and the Integrator. One structural bar for all three. About seven hours.
- [The blind transfer test](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/capstone-blind-transfer.md): A sixty-minute clock, no hints, a domain you have never seen, and one fault planted in its data. Build the course's shapes from a cold start and walk the fault from symptom to root cause. 90 minutes.
- [Capstone Rubric](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/academy/capstone-rubric.md): The five dimensions and four levels your capstone demo is scored against. Certification requires Solid or better on all five.

## Concepts

- [Solutions and Harnesses](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/harnesses.md): How one outcome-owned solution maps to the harness runtime boundary, its lifecycle, and its selection by the dashboard, API, and channels.
- [Sovereign, Transparent AI](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/sovereign-transparent-ai.md): Why Cavelon is built ground-up on three principles — you control where data is processed, can see and prove what every agent does, and can gate and review every layer of the stack.
- [Layered Control](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/layered-control.md): The third pillar — every layer, from backend config and the agent graph down to tool calls, Solution Library entries, and text blocks, is a checkpoint you can gate, validate, review, log, and pin.
- [Anatomy of a Run](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/anatomy-of-a-run.md): How a single message becomes an answer — the end-to-end lifecycle of one chatbot turn, from inbound message to streamed reply, and the engines, checks, and records that make it happen.
- [The Agent Graph](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/agent-graph.md): How Cavelon runs a graph of specialized agents in one conversation — the execution loop, handoffs, consults, and proven topology patterns.
- [Hybrid Orchestration](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/hybrid-orchestration.md): Mix agentic agents with deterministic pipeline nodes in one graph — the node catalog, edge types, data lanes, fan-out, and the Node Workbench
- [Run State](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/run-state.md): Run-scoped, schema-validated shared state for agent runs - design the schema, wire agents and triggers, map tool results, and read the event timeline.
- [Context Budgets](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/context-budgets.md): How much of a model's window each call may use, how that number is worked out, and what happens when the material does not fit
- [Capacity and Concurrency](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/capacity-and-concurrency.md): Every limit that decides how much work runs at once — model endpoint slots, run caps, branches inside a run, ingestion and rate limits — what waits, what is refused, and where each one is set and seen
- [Ordered knowledge bases](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/kb-orders.md): How a source system declares a corpus and how agents answer about it — the two harnesses, why each is a single agent, and what the corpus rules are.
- [Triggers](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/triggers.md): Run your agent graph on a schedule, from a webhook, from inbound email, or from a calendar event - no live user in the chat
- [Documents](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/documents.md): The top-down view of document processing — one identity, three storage worlds, five access mechanisms, and three lifecycle legs (understand, author, deliver) across chat, webhook, email, KB, and cloud
- [Prompt Composition](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/prompt-composition.md): How Cavelon assembles each agent's final system prompt — the real ordered set of sections, what each contributes, when each is skipped, and the request lifecycle.
- [Solution Library Complete Guide](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/workflow-catalog.md): Set up, discover, review, install, adapt, publish, maintain, retire, and recover governed workflow building blocks and solution blueprints
- [Text Blocks](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/text-blocks.md): Reuse approved deterministic wording in transform, output, join, and document templates without asking an agent to reproduce it
- [Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/human-in-the-loop.md): Put a human in front of consequential actions — the end user confirms in chat, an admin approves from the dashboard, or your own system approves over the API.
- [Personas](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/personas.md): The Persona page defines WHO your assistant is — identity, greeting, response style, language, citation and image policy, and the widget copy users see.
- [Knowledge Bases and Retrieval](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/knowledge-bases.md): How knowledge bases ingest, store, and retrieve content through the four-stage contextual retrieval pipeline.
- [Knowledge Base Ingestion](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/kb-ingestion.md): How content enters a knowledge base — web scraping, file uploads, and text and FAQ entries — and how it is processed, synced, and recovered
- [Structured Knowledge Bases](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/structured-kbs.md): Turn a flat table of records into a filterable, semantically searchable catalog your agents query with typed parameters and present as carousels and detail cards
- [Tools](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/tools.md): How agents take action beyond text — builtin capabilities, webhook integrations, MCP attachment, audit, and secret safety
- [Document Access Model](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/document-access-model.md): Where documents live and how an agent reaches them — the three storage worlds, the five access mechanisms, and the asymmetries that trip up mental models
- [Sharing Knowledge Bases Across Tenants](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/cross-tenant-kb-sharing.md): Share one knowledge base read-only with a linked tenant through explicit grants, without copying data or weakening tenant isolation.
- [Tool Templates](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/tool-templates.md): How a tenant binds a shared platform tool template — supplying its own secrets, variables, and overrides — instead of copying it
- [Skills](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/skills.md): Reusable workflow bundles that layer instructions, tools, and knowledge bases onto an agent without adding a graph node
- [Agent Memory](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/memory.md): How agents remember facts and past conversations across sessions — what recall selects and why, continuity through open threads, identity requirements, retention, and configuration
- [Attachments](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/attachments.md): How every attachment — image, document, or audio — enters the harness through one store and one descriptor, branches by kind, and reaches every consumer the same way
- [Guardrails](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/guardrails.md): Content-safety rules that screen agent input and output — classifier, pattern, and webhook types, direction, assignment, and the built-in guardrails
- [Connections](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/connections.md): Tenant OAuth accounts for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, reused by email, calendar, cloud files, and MCP — plus per-user delegated OAuth
- [Choosing Models](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/choosing-models.md): Strategy for picking the right model per agent role — capability tiers, temperature, reasoning, vision, latency, and cost
- [Playground and Debugging](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/playground-and-debugging.md): Test chat and harness runs with live traces, step-by-step Workbench debugging, data rails, side-effect controls, retrieval, memory, and run state.
- [AI Wizards](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/ai-wizards.md): How Harness Architect designs and repairs whole harnesses, and how the Persona Wizard generates your bot's identity
- [Regression Testing](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/concepts/regression-testing.md): Build suites of reference Q&A, run them through your live agent graph, score answers with an LLM judge, and compare runs to catch regressions.

## Channels & Integration

- [Channels Overview](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/overview.md): The menu of ways to connect Cavelon to the world — widget, chat API, KB search, voice, telephony, email, triggers — and how to choose
- [Messaging channels](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/messaging-channels.md): Set up, test and manage conversation channels, or connect your own transport through a webhook
- [Author a channel](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/authoring-channels.md): Build your own no-code catalog channel with a manifest — signature, field mapping, and reply template — plus the dry-run tester and the review-and-allowlist flow
- [Chat Widget](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/widget.md): Embed, theme, and configure the hosted Cavelon chat widget on any website with a single script tag and a chat-scoped key
- [Chat API](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/chat-api.md): Integrate Cavelon into custom apps with a streaming, multi-agent chat endpoint — authentication, conversation lifecycle, SSE events, and production guidance
- [Build a chat client](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/build-a-chat-client.md): Checklist for shipping your own chat front end — one full turn, then citations, attachments, approvals, cancellation, and the stability guarantees to build on
- [KB Search API](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/kb-search-api.md): Query knowledge bases directly for ranked chunks or filtered records — authentication, prose and structured search, response shapes, and retrieval tuning
- [Chat User Authentication](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/end-user-auth.md): Sign Chat Users in with enterprise SSO, email OTP, or a personal cloud account, and bind their verified identity to conversations and knowledge access
- [Uploads and Images](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/uploads-and-images.md): Let visitors attach images to chat and upload their own documents — the channel setup, the upload experience, admin monitoring, quotas, and security
- [Realtime Voice](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/voice.md): Add a live, spoken browser conversation to your bot — OpenAI Realtime over WebRTC or a self-hosted Qwen3 pipeline over WebSocket
- [Telephony](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/telephony.md): Connect your voice agent to real phone numbers — multi-tenant routing, Twilio, Vonage, and FreeSWITCH, call transfer with schedules, and the audio bridge
- [Email Channels](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/email.md): Run business inboxes through Cavelon — connect a mailbox, trigger agent runs from inbound mail, process attachments, and send guarded replies
- [Calendar](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/calendar.md): Give agents a real Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace calendar — book, update, and cancel meetings, find free slots, and react when the calendar changes
- [MCP Servers](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/mcp-servers.md): Connect agents to many tools at once through Model Context Protocol servers — remote or local, OAuth-authenticated, catalog-installed, and governed
- [Enterprise Integration](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/channels/enterprise-integration.md): An architecture guide for solution architects — deployment models, patterns for connecting internal systems, security layers, and a phased rollout

## Administration

- [Transparency Controls and Audit](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/ai-transparency.md): The operational hub for seeing and controlling what an agent does to enterprise data — before, during, and after it acts — and where your data goes, organized as an auditor's checklist.
- [Conversations](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/conversations.md): Browse, search, filter, and inspect chat conversations — transcripts, traces, retrieval, memory, ratings, and export
- [GDPR Compliance](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/gdpr.md): How Cavelon capabilities map onto GDPR — controller/processor roles, data-subject rights, retention, consent, breach response, encryption, and transfers
- [Access Control and RBAC](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/access-control-rbac.md): The canonical model for Platform Users, Tenant Memberships, Chat Users, Academy grants, role scopes, and fine-grained permissions.
- [Platform Users and Tenant Members](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/admin-members.md): Understand dashboard identities, tenant memberships, invitations, lifecycle controls, and the boundary with Chat Users and Academy learners.
- [Retrieval Models](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/retrieval-models.md): Configure Platform and tenant embedding and reranker policies, test providers, and migrate vector indexes safely
- [API Keys and Authentication](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/api-keys-and-auth.md): How the platform authenticates programmatic clients with scoped API keys and the admin dashboard with JWT cookies, plus tenant context and rate limits
- [Administrative Audit Log](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/audit-log.md): How the administrative evidence trail works, what makes it enterprise-ready, and how it connects to AI runtime transparency.
- [EU AI Act Compliance](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/eu-ai-act.md): How Cavelon aligns with the EU AI Act — risk tiers, transparency duties, human oversight, logging and traceability, governance, and the compliance timeline
- [Audit Log for Tenant Teams](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/audit-log-tenant.md): Tenant-scoped investigations, evidence exports, common use cases, and practical audit tips.
- [Personal Access Tokens](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/personal-access-tokens.md): Your own credential for scripts, CI and the Cavelon dev-kit — creating one, what its ceiling means, and how a tenant or platform administrator revokes it
- [Analytics](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/analytics.md): One customer-facing view of usage, answer quality, security, technical state, costs, and uploads — with traceable definitions and conversation drill-downs
- [Chat Users and Groups](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/chat-users-and-groups.md): The Chat User access model — invitations, tenant sign-in, manual and SSO groups, and knowledge-base retrieval gates.
- [Shared Responsibility Model](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/shared-responsibility.md): The compliance boundary between what the Cavelon platform provides and what you, the tenant, must configure and operate for GDPR and the EU AI Act
- [Sandboxes on Your Own VM](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/sandbox-runner.md): What a Sandbox is for, where your files stay, and how to connect your VM step by step
- [Memory Explorer](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/memory-explorer.md): Inspect, curate, and prune what your chatbot remembers about individual contacts — KPIs, charts, evidence, version history, and GDPR erasure
- [Privacy Configuration](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/privacy-configuration.md): A step-by-step guide to configuring Cavelon's privacy and data-protection controls — retention, PII guardrails, AI disclosure, subject requests, and encryption
- [Two-Factor Authentication](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/two-factor-auth.md): Time-based one-time-password MFA for admin dashboard accounts — enrollment, recovery codes, tenant enforcement policy, and admin recovery
- [Usage & Costs](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/usage-and-costs.md): Inspect Processing-Step activity and Runs in every mode, plus cost evidence where the Billing runtime permits it
- [Settings](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/settings.md): A section-by-section tour of tenant Settings — models and retrieval, memory and documents, limits and usage, and security and access
- [Third-Party Data Flows](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/third-party-data-flows.md): Every external service that can receive data from Cavelon — what is sent, the controls available, and the self-hosting alternative for each one
- [Model Registry](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/model-registry.md): Manage generative and voice models — provider presets, registered models, role defaults, and reasoning configuration in one place.
- [Support Boundaries](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/support-boundaries.md): What tenant roles can configure independently versus what needs platform-operator, instance-owner, or vendor support
- [Governance and Action Permissions](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/governance.md): Control what agents may do in connected systems with allow, approval, and deny policies — tenant-wide, per group, or per end user.
- [Curating the Solution Library](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/workflow-catalog-curation.md): Operate Publisher Studio, package review, marketplace moderation, visibility, guard rules, release lifecycle, and the application trace
- [Notifications](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/notifications.md): Personal Inbox, unified delivery settings, member defaults, and delivery troubleshooting.
- [Incident Response](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/administration/incident-response.md): Work major incidents, inspect correlated monitoring signals, and configure accountable central and tenant response routes.

## Reference

- [Configuration Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/configuration.md): Every environment variable the platform reads at startup, with defaults and tuning guidance, grouped by subsystem.
- [Retrieval Parameters Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/retrieval-parameters.md): Every knob in the contextual retrieval pipeline — hybrid search, reranking, thresholds, context budget, and language — with defaults, ranges, and effects
- [Nodes and Edges Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/nodes-and-edges.md): The exhaustive per-node and per-edge field catalog for the orchestration graph — node types, edge types, condition operators, API Request, Tool Call, and MCP Tool Call
- [Built-in Tools Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/builtin-tools.md): The complete catalog of built-in agent tools — document search and write, web search, compute, forms, website guide links, calendar, email, Personal Assistant, and experimental sub-agents
- [Agent Action Catalog](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/action-catalog.md): Every data-touching action an agent can take, classified read, write, or delete for governance — the authoritative inventory behind allow/approval/deny policies.
- [Structured Data Preparation](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/structured-data-preparation.md): Prepare, validate, and export relational data as a portable SQLite file for a structured knowledge base
- [Webhook Tool Definition](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/webhook-definition.md): The complete schema for webhook tools — URL, method, headers, template placeholders, parameter and response mapping, timeouts, retries, and schema auto-discovery
- [API Endpoints Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/api-endpoints.md): Exhaustive reference for every public API-key endpoint — chat, knowledge-base search, and voice — with auth scopes, request fields, responses, and error codes
- [Citations and artifacts](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/citations-and-artifacts.md): How a custom chat client turns an answer's sources into links — the download: and upload: ref schemes, the sources chip array, the artifacts array, and the endpoints that serve a cited document
- [KB Management API](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/kb-management-api.md): Programmatically create and configure knowledge bases, ingest and manage documents, run web scraping, and drive structured-data KBs — auth scopes, request and response shapes, and curl examples.
- [Server-Sent Events](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/sse-events.md): The complete Server-Sent Events catalog for streaming chat — every event name, when it fires, and its payload fields, with a worked consumer example
- [Widget Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/widget-reference.md): Every attribute, theming CSS variable, authentication handoff, and supported event for the chatbot-widget and chatbot-voice custom elements
- [Trigger Payloads and Callbacks](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/trigger-payloads.md): The exhaustive wire contract for trigger webhooks - inbound request shape, payload-to-input and Run State mapping, the runtime trigger payload, and outbound callbacks
- [Limits and Quotas](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/limits-and-quotas.md): Consolidated reference for upload, file size, chunking, message, history, rate, timeout, and image limits across every scope
- [Text Blocks & Workflow Catalog Reference](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/text-blocks-and-catalog.md): Field-level reference behind Text Blocks and the Solution Library — markers, state machines, marketplace fields, permissions, installation contracts, and API surface
- [Glossary](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/reference/glossary.md): Alphabetical definitions of Cavelon platform terms, each linking to its home page in the docs

## Troubleshooting

- [Common Issues](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/troubleshooting/common-issues.md): A symptom-to-fix catalog for chat, the agent graph, knowledge bases, webhooks, Pricing and Billing, the dashboard, performance, and snapshots
- [Best Practices](https://cavelon.example.com/api/v1/docs/troubleshooting/best-practices.md): Opinionated patterns for agent design, reusable solutions, knowledge bases, prompts, tools, security, performance, memory, testing, and automation
